title: Mango Pulp Weevil: The Quarantine Pest of Palawan
metaTitle: Mango Pulp Weevil: Damage, Quarantine and Control
metaDescription: The mango pulp weevil is a quarantine pest found in Palawan that tunnels in the fruit. Learn the damage, the movement ban and why it matters for exports.
excerpt: The mango pulp weevil, Sternochetus frigidus, is a small dark weevil whose grubs eat the pulp of mango fruit from inside. In the Philippines it is found in the Palawan island group, and the BPI keeps the rest of the country protected by quarantine. This page explains the damage and what a mango farmer should do.

blocks.text:
The adult is a dark brown, small, stout weevil with paler patches and a small head. Scales cover the body. A female lays single eggs on young fruit, and the grub bores into the pulp. The grub is the most destructive stage, because it feeds and develops in the pulp.

It feeds only on mango, whatever the variety. It was first found in the Philippines in 1987, probably brought from Borneo to southern Palawan. The BPI declared it a dangerous pest and placed the Palawan island group under quarantine. As the rest of the country is free of it, most mango farmers never see it, and they must help to keep it out.

blocks.caption: Quick facts
rows: It attacks developing fruit, and the damage stays hidden until the fruit is cut open at harvest.

The female lays single eggs on young fruit and covers each with a plug. An egg hatches in about 9 days, the grub grows over about 20 days, and the new adult stays inside the fruit for about 37 days more.

blocks.text: How to Identify Mango Pulp Weevil

You cannot see the damage on the outside before harvest. Cut the fruit open and look for darkened tunnels in the pulp, grubs and adult weevils inside. The [mango cecid fly](/pests/mango-cecid-fly) leaves spots on the skin, while the pulp weevil works inside. If you find a weevil in a fruit outside Palawan, report it to the BPI or the provincial agriculture office.

items: Tunnels in the pulp darken the flesh after the grub feeds.
Grubs and adult weevils are found inside the cut fruit.
The outside of the fruit looks normal until harvest.
Adults feed on the mango flowers during bloom.
The fruit comes from or passed through Palawan.

blocks.title: Do not confuse it with
blocks.text: Fruit rot and tunnels from other insects can look similar inside. The [oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly) leaves maggots in the pulp, while the pulp weevil leaves a hard bodied grub and adult weevils.
How Mango Pulp Weevil Hurts Your Crop

The weevil is a quarantine pest, and it stopped the export of Philippine mangoes to some countries. Mangoes from Guimaras Island are certified pest free and have an exemption. A study at UPLB found that irradiation above 75 Gy sterilized insects treated in the early stages and above 100 Gy sterilized the adults. Irradiation is now a post harvest treatment for export fruit.

The BPI reports that no eradication measure is available. So the main aim is to stop its spread. The quarantine bans the movement of mango plants, fruit and parts out of Palawan. A farm outside Palawan that breaks this rule risks both its own fruit and the whole country's export market.
How to Control Mango Pulp Weevil

items: Follow the movement ban. Do not carry mango plants, fruits or parts out of the Palawan island group.
Buy planting material only from registered nurseries and never from an infested area.
In Palawan, pick up and destroy fallen fruit so the grubs and the new adults do not escape.
Check cut fruit for tunnels and grubs at harvest, and report any find outside Palawan to the BPI.
Ask the BPI about the approved export treatment, which is irradiation, if you grow mango for the export market.

blocks.text: No spray is recommended in the sources we read. The control is the quarantine and post harvest irradiation for export fruit, not an insecticide in the orchard.

blocks.title: Spray safely
blocks.text: Use only products registered with the [Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority](/blog/fertilizer-and-pesticide-authority), and follow the label for the rate, the timing and the protective clothing. Switch to a different insecticide group next time, so the pest does not learn to survive it. Our [guide to integrated pest management](/pests/integrated-pest-management) explains how.

items: Never bring mango fruit or seedlings out of Palawan.
Report any weevil or tunneled pulp you find outside Palawan.
Use only registered nurseries and certified material.
Cooperate with BPI inspectors at quarantine checkpoints.

blocks.text: Questions Farmers Ask About Mango Pulp Weevil

items.q: Where is the mango pulp weevil in the Philippines?
items.a: In certain areas of the Palawan island group. The BPI declared the pest dangerous and placed Palawan under quarantine.

items.q: Can I take mangoes out of Palawan?
items.a: No. The quarantine bans the movement of mango plants, fruits or parts out of the Palawan island group.
It is a quarantine pest for countries with strict import rules. Guimaras mangoes are certified pest free, and irradiation is also used on export fruit.
